1. **Assessment & planning:** Inventory the 2 TB database (schema, extensions, roles, sequences), select the target managed service (matching Postgres version/extensions), size compute/storage/IOPS for the workload, and produce a runbook with a minute-by-minute timeline that fits the 2-hour Sunday window.
2. **Stakeholder communication (initial):** Notify engineering, support, and end users at least 1 week ahead of the maintenance window (date/time, expected read-only or downtime period), with reminders at 48h and 1h before, and a designated status-update channel during the migration.
3. **Environment setup:** Provision the managed Postgres instance, configure networking/VPC peering or VPN, security groups, IAM/roles, parameter groups, and encryption to mirror or improve on-prem settings.
4. **Non-production dry run:** Take a full backup/snapshot of production, restore it into a staging copy (or use a scrubbed/representative dataset), and rehearse the entire migration (backup, transfer, restore, cutover, verification, rollback) end-to-end against the managed service; record timings to confirm the process fits the 2-hour window.
5. **Refine runbook from rehearsal:** Fix issues found in the dry run (slow steps, compatibility errors, extension mismatches), and re-time each phase; if the rehearsal doesn't fit the window, plan a pre-seed strategy (initial bulk copy days ahead + final delta sync) instead of a single full 2TB transfer.
6. **Pre-cutover replication seed (before window):** Days before the maintenance window, take a full backup of the production database, then start continuous logical replication/CDC (e.g., pg_logical, AWS DMS, or native logical replication) from on-prem to the managed target so only a small delta remains at cutover time.
7. **Final stakeholder notice & freeze:** At the start of the maintenance window, confirm go-ahead with stakeholders, announce the start of the maintenance window to users, and put the application into read-only/maintenance mode to stop new writes.
8. **Final full backup:** Immediately before any destructive/modifying action on production, take one last full backup (pg_dump/pg_basebackup or snapshot) of the on-prem database and verify it completes successfully and is restorable.
9. **Final sync & cutover:** Apply the last replication delta (or final incremental dump/restore) to the managed target so it is fully caught up, then repoint application connection strings/DNS/secrets to the new managed database and restart application services.
10. **Data integrity verification:** Compare row counts per table, checksums (e.g., `pg_checksums`/`checksum` extension or `md5` hash aggregates), sequence values, and index/constraint counts between source backup and target; block go-live until verification passes.
11. **Go-live & monitoring:** Take the application out of maintenance mode, monitor query performance, replication lag, error rates, and connection health closely for the remainder of the window and the following 24–48 hours; send stakeholders a completion/status update.
12. **Rollback procedure (trigger at any failure point in steps 7–11):** Take the application back into maintenance mode, repoint connection strings/DNS back to the original on-prem server (kept fully intact and untouched throughout), replay any writes made against the new database (if any) back into on-prem using captured delta logs, verify on-prem integrity via the same row-count/checksum checks, resume traffic on-prem, and notify stakeholders of the rollback and revised migration timeline.

STEP COUNT: 12
